reason: The text opens with 'Then Moses sang...and the children of Israel sang this song' (אָ֣ז יָשִֽׁיר־ מֹשֶׁה֩ וּבְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל), establishing Moses as the initiator and leader of the people in a collective act. While the Song of the Sea (Shirat ha-Yam) primarily celebrates God's military and redemptive power, Moses is portrayed in the leadership position of guiding and directing the entire nation's religious response. He stands before the people (not with them as an equal) and leads them in communal worship. This positioning, combined with his prior role in the exodus narrative, confirms his status as the established national leader of Israel at this moment in the text.
